name: Haircut Number Two Hundred
why_it_works: A visit count is loyalty made visible. Watching one regular across years makes the place feel like a home, not a transaction, and newcomers want to belong to something that lasts. The number in the hook is oddly specific, so people stop to read it.

hook.pattern: Lead with a large, specific visit number for one regular, then jump back to visit one.
examples: This is Marcus's 214th haircut in this chair.
Visit #1 to visit #{{visit_count}}. Same guy. Same chair.
We've cut his hair through three jobs and two kids.

variables.name: regular_name
variables.description: First name of the regular, with permission

variables.name: visit_count
variables.description: Their visit number, a real figure

variables.name: first_visit_detail
variables.description: What the first visit looked like
variables.example: he wanted a fade for prom

variables.name: life_moment
variables.description: A life moment the shop was part of

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of a regular customer in the chair at {{brand}}, mirror reflection, warm tungsten light, barber's hands mid-cut, candid
Vertical photo styled like an old snapshot, slightly faded film look, the same chair at {{brand}} years ago, younger customer, flash photography
Vertical photo inside {{brand}}, a celebratory or tender moment between barber and customer, a handshake or hug, soft window light

beats.purpose: the turn: the chair as a constant
beats.voiceover: Jobs changed. Neighborhoods changed. The chair didn't.

visual.prompt: Slow orbit around an empty barber chair at {{brand}} at closing time, warm light, slight haze, vertical 9:16

craft.notes: Shoot or generate the past as an old snapshot so time passing is visible at a glance. The constant object (the chair) carries the theme; the people change around it. End on the empty chair so the viewer imagines sitting in it.

do_not: Use a regular without asking them
Overload with every life event; pick one
